_comment_rankings: McGill's ranks, each with its source, its edition and a link to the ranking itself. Re-check every June, when QS publishes a new edition. The text may only repeat what the items say, and always names the source: '#1 in Canada' is true for QS, not for every ranking.

rankings.headline: You study where university students study.
rankings.text: In its 2027 edition, QS ranks McGill University #1 in Canada. In the world, it is #30. For finance research, the 2026 EduRank ranking places it #3 in Canada.

_comment_testimonials: Real answers from ONE former student of Ilyas's previous finance class (summer 2026, not an AIM class). Only typos are fixed; a cut is marked […]; never add a word, a name, a school or a photo. The student's written OK is kept in the private 'AIM — preuves' folder, not here.

testimonials.source: Student — took Ilyas's previous finance class, summer 2026
testimonials.short: […] I was expecting a monotone class about finance and stocks. I was completely wrong, the class I took with Ilyas was the opposite of that and was anything but boring.

items.label: The surprise
items.quote: Before my first day at McGill, I was expecting a monotone class about finance and stocks. I was completely wrong, the class I took with Ilyas was the opposite of that and was anything but boring.

items.label: The teacher
items.quote: During my classes under his guidance, Ilyas proved to me that he had our success at heart by constantly checking up on us and making sure we understood. He would often take extra time after class to discuss further with students and answer questions.

items.label: What stuck
items.quote: I can confidently say that the knowledge I gained with Ilyas is what leads me to understand the value of the market, know how to seize valuable opportunities and better manage my money.

_comment_apply: The guided application (apply.html). Everything below is shown as options in the form; flip a session to "waitlist" when it is full, set a level's "from" year to open it. Values (ids) must match the Edge Function submit-application. The FinTech program (id "fintech-digital-investing") is not in the form while it is only a 2028 waitlist: its card on the home page opens an email instead. Add it back here the day it has dates. A session gets its "Save the date" button the day it has confirmed "start" and "end" dates (format 2027-06-28).

lessons.title: Finance basics
lessons.teaser: What finance really is, saving vs. investing, budgeting, compound interest, inflation, risk and return.

lessons.title: Stock market basics
lessons.teaser: What a stock is, how the TSX and Wall Street work, indexes, ETFs, dividends, bull and bear markets, diversification.

lessons.title: How to start investing in Canada
lessons.teaser: TFSA, RRSP, FHSA and RESP explained, choosing a broker, buying your first ETF in 5 steps, mistakes and scams to avoid.

levels.name: Beginner
levels.learn: How money really works, how the stock market moves, how to read a company, and how to build a portfolio — value, growth, momentum and diversification.
levels.capstoneDetail: A simulated $1,000,000 portfolio on a virtual stock exchange — one strategy, defined and defended in front of the class.

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.learn: The economy and the markets, bonds, ETFs and asset allocation, measuring risk, valuation (DCF), moats, market history and factor investing.
levels.capstoneDetail: Run a $1,000,000 multi-asset portfolio with a written investment policy, a benchmark and a risk scorecard — and present it to an investment committee.

levels.name: Advanced
levels.course: Advanced Investment Management: How the Pros Invest
levels.learn: How Wall Street works, options and futures, rates and currencies, quantitative investing, hedge funds, private markets, risk management and AI.
levels.capstoneDetail: Design a professional strategy, run it on $1,000,000 with written risk limits and a trading journal — then pitch it to a mock investment committee.
